version.changelog: Sync existing infra403/opentwitter-mcp from https://github.com/6551Team/opentwitter-mcp, main commit 8d69ca5e856f2026fde6b1903f6e06d63bab0770, directory openclaw-skill/opentwitter. Exact upstream SKILL.md and package.json; generated skill-card.md excluded. Adds meme token evidence/activity documentation and watch groupName parameter. Existing owner, slug and display name preserved. No example commands executed.

llm.summary: This is mostly a documented Twitter/X data client, but it also supports deleted-content retrieval and persistent account monitoring that users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: Credentialed network calls to https://ai.6551.io are expected for this API skill, but those calls transmit search terms, usernames, tweet IDs, watchlist changes, and the bearer token to the provider.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation metadata only requires curl and a user-provided OPENNEWS_TOKEN; no local executable payload, dependency package, service, hook, or startup mechanism was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The endpoints are explicit and user-invoked, but the manifest and package summary understate ongoing monitoring and real-time streaming, and the documentation lacks privacy, consent, or acceptable-use guidance for sensitive social graph and deleted-content features.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can add and delete monitored Twitter accounts through provider API calls, creating persistent server-side monitoring state and enabling real-time event streams until removed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose broadly fits Twitter/X and meme data access, but the artifact also documents deleted tweet retrieval, follower/unfollower event lookup, provider-side watchlist management, and WebSocket streaming of monitored account activity.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the 6551/OpenNews service with your bearer token and the Twitter/X accounts, searches, tweet IDs, and monitoring lists you submit. Treat deleted-tweet, follower-event, watchlist, and WebSocket features as sensitive monitoring tools, and remove watched accounts when monitoring is no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the body discloses the monitoring features, but the top-level description does not clearly mention watchlist management or WebSocket streaming.
[E1] expected: Most external POST requests are expected for a credentialed API skill; they are not exfiltration by themselves, but they do send user queries and identifiers to the 6551 service.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: deleted tweet retrieval, follower/unfollower events, watchlists, and streaming are privacy-impacting capabilities presented without meaningful user-facing safeguards or usage limits.
[SDI-2] expected: The OPENNEWS_TOKEN requirement is clearly declared in the skill metadata and authentication section, so credentialed access is expected for this provider integration.
